pegasus-project-spyware-2021.summary: On 18 July 2021 a consortium of 17 news organisations coordinated by Forbidden Stories, with Amnesty International's Security Lab, publishes Pegasus Project: a leaked list of 50,000 phone numbers selected by government clients of Israeli firm NSO Group, and forensic proof of Pegasus infections on phones of journalists, activists, lawyers and a murdered Saudi journalist's fiancée. Amnesty's methodology report, peer-reviewed by Citizen Lab, documents zero-click iMessage exploits defeating fully patched iPhones and releases an open-source Mobile Verification Toolkit. US Commerce Department blacklists NSO in November 2021, Apple sues, and Israel tightens export licences, while spyware market shifts to rivals such as Predator.

rtss-malaria-vaccine-who-2021.summary: After 30 years of development by GlaxoSmithKline with PATH, and a phase 3 trial in 15,459 children at 11 African sites showing 36 percent fewer clinical malaria cases over four years with a booster, RTS,S was piloted from 2019 in Ghana, Kenya and Malawi. On 6 October 2021 WHO recommended it for children in regions of moderate to high transmission, a first for any vaccine against a parasite; Director-General Tedros called it "a historic moment". Pilots in 900,000 children showed a 13 percent fall in all-cause mortality. In October 2023 WHO added R21/Matrix-M from Oxford and the Serum Institute of India, whose phase 3 trial in 4,800 children gave 75 percent efficacy at seasonal sites. By February 2026, 25 African countries were vaccinating, aiming at over 10 million children a year, where more than 260,000 under-fives die of malaria annually.

sanatech-gaba-tomato-2021.summary: In September 2021 Tokyo start-up Sanatech Seed, working with Tsukuba University, begins commercial sales of Sicilian Rouge High GABA tomatoes, edited with CRISPR-Cas9 to truncate the autoinhibitory domain of glutamate decarboxylase so fruit holds about five times normal gamma-aminobutyric acid, marketed for blood pressure. Japan's Ministry of Health accepted notification in December 2020 under rules treating edits without foreign DNA as conventional breeding, so no safety review or GM label applied, and seedlings went to home gardeners in May 2021. sri-lanka-fertilizer-ban-2021.summary: In April 2021 President Gotabaya Rajapaksa banned imports of synthetic fertiliser and agrochemicals, ordering an immediate switch to organic farming for all two million farmers, partly to save foreign exchange. Organic substitutes were unavailable at scale. Paddy output in 2021-22 maha season fell by roughly a fifth to a third, tea exports dropped, and rice imports and food inflation followed. Government reversed ban in November 2021 and paid compensation, but losses fed into 2022 economic collapse and protests that forced Rajapaksa out. Case became a reference point on agronomic limits of abrupt organic transitions and on nutrient budgeting for small farms.
